EFW_Theo.name: Theo
EFW_Theo.role: Junior attaché and field cartography worker whose impossible memories lead him to the buried war
EFW_Theo.notes: Obsessive, intuitive and increasingly frightened by recognition. Theo has dreamed places, gestures and events that should not exist in his life. He is not an engineer explaining anomalies; he is a person trying to prove that impossible memories are real. His recurring thumb-to-index-finger motion evokes holding an absent tactical stylus, but it should appear only when emotionally meaningful.

EFW_Rae.name: Rae
EFW_Rae.role: Zenith Spire archivist who discovers suppressed evidence of the forgotten history returning
EFW_Rae.notes: Incisive, skeptical and self-controlled. Rae notices patterns, omissions and institutional behavior. She resists panic by tracing simple shapes against her thigh, a private grounding habit rather than a technical calculation. Her strength is deciding what evidence means politically and personally, not diagnosing phenomena.

EFW_Adrian.name: Adrian
EFW_Adrian.role: Neutral envoy and antiquarian who recognizes the forgotten war and fears its return
EFW_Adrian.notes: Restrained, burdened, evasively knowledgeable. Adrian often knows what a discovery means but refuses to say why. His authority comes from memory, history and consequence. He never speaks like a clinician, engineer or risk assessor. He is frightened most by recognition.

EFW_Vark.name: Vark
EFW_Vark.notes: Practical, experienced, dry and humane. Vark is the ordinary-world contrast to Theo: he thinks about shifts, injuries, workers, bosses and what happens tomorrow. He can be funny without becoming comic relief and skeptical without becoming a compliance officer.

EFW_Caelum.name: Caelum
EFW_Caelum.notes: Institutional, political and controlling. Caelum protects order, secrecy and his own authority. He is more interested in who is allowed to know something than in technical explanation. His conflict with Rae is about control of truth.
